top.title: 2027: US providing real-time intelligence to Nigerian military against terrorists — Musa
top.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigeria’s Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa, has said the United States is providing real-time intelligence, satellite imagery and training to the Nigerian military to track and target terrorist leaders ahead of the 2027 general elections. According to Reuters, Musa disclosed this on Monday during a briefing with journalists, saying the improved intelligence support had strengthened the military’s ability to identify and strike militant targets. The minister said Nigerian troops had killed several terrorist and bandit leaders in overnight operations in the Northwest and Northeast, adding that the military was conducting almost daily operations with improved intelligence. “We took out a lot of the bandit leaders and the terrorists themselves,” Musa said. He said Nigeria and the United States had continued to expand their security cooperation as the country battles Islamist insurgencies in the North-East, armed banditry in the North-West and kidnapping gangs across the country. Musa also disclosed that Nigeria was expecting additional military helicopters from the United States and Italy to strengthen its operational capacity. On preparations for the 2027 general elections, the defence minister said security agencies were intensifying intelligence-led operations to prevent violence before, during and after the polls. He said authorities were also monitoring the use of Starlink satellite internet services, cryptocurrencies and commercial drones by militant groups, while working with US authorities to disrupt their financing networks. Musa further disclosed that Nigeria had reached a five-kilometre cross-border right-of-pursuit arrangement with Cameroon, Niger and Chad, allowing troops to pursue terrorists and bandits across border areas. The arrangement is aimed at restricting the movement of armed groups that exploit porous borders to escape security operations. The minister also warned that Islamic State Sahel was seeking to recruit criminal gangs in North-West Nigeria, raising concerns that largely profit-driven bandit groups could develop into ideologically driven insurgent organisations similar to the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP). According to him, militants and bandits have continued to exploit dense forests and porous borders with Niger and Benin to evade security forces after carrying out attacks. However, he said improved surveillance had strengthened the military’s ability to track armed groups through difficult terrain and restricted their freedom of movement. “We don’t want them to develop that capacity,” Musa said. “We’re blocking the logistics and taking them out from within Nigeria.” The post 2027: US providing real-time intelligence to Nigerian military against terrorists — Musa appeared first on Vanguard News .

top.title: FG introduces NIN-linked verification system for domestic air passengers
top.description: The Federal Government has introduced a biometric passenger verification system linked to the National Identification Number (NIN) for domestic air travel, in a move aimed at strengthening airport security and curbing identity fraud. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Tuesday after unveiling the Airport Passenger Verification System, known as V-PASS, at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos. Keyamo said the system would make it mandatory for passengers on domestic flights to verify their identities using their NIN before boarding. He explained that the technology was designed to eliminate cases of passengers travelling with fake identities, as well as address touting and ticket racketeering at airports. According to him, the biometric identity verification system would enhance passenger processing, strengthen airport security and provide a faster and more seamless travel experience. The minister said the project was executed through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) arrangement. He was accompanied at the unveiling by the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN), Mrs Olubunmi Kuku; Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), Dr Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh; and other senior FAAN officials. Keyamo said he had directed the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) to give all airlines operating in the country until December 31 to integrate with the system. He clarified that the verification system was designed exclusively for domestic flights. top.title: Tinubu: Nigerians can access ₦100m mortgages at 9.75%
top.description: President Bola Tinubu has said eligible Nigerians can access mortgage loans of up to ₦100 million at a fixed interest rate of 9.75 per cent under the Federal Government’s ₦1 trillion MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund (MREIF). Tinubu, who disclosed this in a post on his X platform on Tuesday, said the initiative was designed to expand access to affordable, long-term housing finance and help more Nigerians become homeowners. He explained that beneficiaries could repay the loans over a period of up to 20 years, with an initial deposit of 10 per cent. Illustrating the arrangement, the President said a Nigerian seeking to purchase a house worth ₦10 million would need an initial deposit of ₦1 million and could repay approximately ₦85,400 monthly over 20 years. According to him, more than 2,300 Nigerians across 27 states have so far accessed ₦160 billion in mortgages through MREIF. Tinubu said the Federal Government had also strengthened the Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN), through which eligible Nigerians could access housing loans of up to ₦50 million at six per cent interest, with repayment periods of up to 30 years. He added that contributors to pension schemes could qualify to use up to 25 per cent of their retirement savings towards the initial deposit, while married applicants could submit joint applications with their spouses to improve their chances of accessing higher loan amounts. The President also highlighted the role of the Family Homes Fund in providing affordable housing for Nigerians who cannot afford mortgage arrangements. He said the fund had delivered more than 53 social homes for vulnerable and underserved households. Tinubu further disclosed that the Renewed Hope Social Housing Programme was targeting 77,400 affordable homes across the country. According to him, 100 free homes had been delivered to widows in Kaduna, while another 50 were provided to wives of fallen military personnel in Ibadan. He added that more than 15,000 housing units were under construction nationwide through the Renewed Hope Cities and Estates Programme. The President stressed that access to the housing initiatives should be based on eligibility rather than political connections or religious affiliation. “You should not need to know a minister, a governor or anybody in the Presidential Villa to apply and benefit from these opportunities,” he said. Tinubu maintained that the programmes were open to Nigerians who met the stipulated requirements, irrespective of their location or beliefs. He said providing opportunities for hardworking Nigerians to own homes and secure their families’ future remained an important objective of his administration’s economic reforms. nigeria.title: Enugu Assembly passes bill limiting rent increase to 2%
nigeria.description: … Landlords can only review rent after four years By Chinedu Adonu The Enugu State House of Assembly has passed a bill seeking to protect tenants from arbitrary rent increases by restricting landlords to a maximum two per cent increment every four years. The bill, which scaled its third reading on Tuesday, also provides for a maximum 10 per cent rent increase where a landlord has undertaken reasonable renovation of the property. Its passage followed the consideration of a report presented by a joint House committee comprising the Committees on Housing and Investment, Public Petition, Ethics and Privileges, and Judiciary. The motion for consideration of the report was moved by the member representing Nkanu West Constituency, Hon. Iloabuchi Aniagu, and seconded by the member representing Awgu North Constituency, Rt. Hon. Jane Eneh. Presenting the report, Chairman of the Committee, Rt. Hon. Okey Mbah, who represents Nkanu East Constituency, said the proposed amendment followed extensive consultations with relevant stakeholders. Mbah described the legislation as a major intervention in landlord-tenant relations, saying it was designed to address the exploitation of tenants and ease the burden of securing accommodation in the state. “This bill will subside over 60 per cent of what residents used to pay while trying to secure accommodation,” he said. Following the presentation, the House dissolved into the Committee of the Whole to consider the report alongside the bill before its eventual passage. The Speaker of the House, Rt. Hon. Uche Ugwu, described the legislation as part of the good governance initiatives of the present administration, saying it would give tenants in the state a new lease of life. The bill, titled A Bill for a Law to Amend the Landlord and Tenant Second Amendment Bill, Cap 101, Revised Laws of Enugu State 2024, House Bill No. 3, 2025, passed second reading on March 11, 2026, and subsequently underwent a public hearing on March 26, 2026. With its passage by the Assembly, the bill now awaits the assent of Governor Peter Mbah before it can become law. nigeria.title: Car washer jailed seven years for stealing customer’s Lexus SUV in Enugu
nigeria.description: By Alumona Ukwueze ENUGU—-A 36-year-old car washer, Adah Martins Pius, has been sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment for stealing a customer’s Toyota Lexus 330 SUV in Enugu State. The Enugu State Police Command disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday by its Police Public Relations Officer, SP Daniel Ndukwe. According to the statement, Pius stole the black Lexus SUV on November 5, 2026, after it was entrusted to him by its owner for washing at Fourth Dimension, Enugu. Rather than wash and return the vehicle, the convict, a native of Ugep in Yakurr Local Government Area of Cross River State, allegedly absconded with it and fled to his hometown. Following a complaint by the vehicle’s owner, operatives of the New Haven Police Division deployed technical intelligence to track down and arrest him in Cross River State. The stolen SUV was subsequently recovered on November 11, 2026. The police said Pius was arraigned before the Enugu North Magistrate Court on November 16, 2026, on a one-count charge of stealing. He pleaded guilty to the charge and was convicted and sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment by the court. The Command commended the operatives involved in the investigation and arrest, as well as the court for the speedy dispensation of justice. It reiterated its commitment to sustaining efforts to rid Enugu State of criminal elements and ensure the safety of residents and their property. nigeria.title: Ikeja LG chairman mourns Vanguard Online Editor, Femi Ajasa
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Executive Chairman of Ikeja Local Government, Comrade Akeem Olalekan Dauda, popularly known as AKOD, has commiserated with Vanguard Media Limited, the family and associates of its late Online Editor, Mr Olufemi Finayon Ajasa. Dauda described Ajasa’s death as a painful loss to the media industry and the journalism profession. Ajasa, aged 44, reportedly died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH) after a brief illness. In a condolence message, the council chairman said the late journalist’s dedication, professionalism and contributions to the growth of digital journalism would remain part of his enduring legacy. He described Ajasa as a committed media professional whose career across several reputable media organisations reflected his passion for journalism, pursuit of excellence and determination to contribute to the evolving media landscape. Dauda particularly commiserated with the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the immediate family of the deceased, as well as his friends and professional colleagues. He urged them to take solace in the impactful life and professional contributions of the late journalist. “Take solace in the impactful life and professional contributions of the late Ajasa, whose passing at the age of 44 is a painful reminder of the fragility of life,” he stated. The council chairman also prayed that Almighty God would comfort the bereaved family, grant them the strength to bear the loss and give the deceased eternal rest. nigeria.title: 2027: Ijaw people support Tinubu’s re-election, Diri declares
nigeria.description: ..Commends Tompolo-led campaign movement …Group donates 25 buses for campaign By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Bayelsa State Governor, Douye Diri, has declared that the majority of Ijaw people support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. Diri said he was confident that the Ijaw nation would give Tinubu overwhelming support in the election, describing the President and the people of the Niger Delta as being in the same political boat. The governor spoke during a rally organised by the High Chief Government Ekpemupolo, popularly known as Tompolo, led PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital. He said the Ijaw people, being experienced mariners and navigators, would ensure that the political boat sailed to victory. Diri listed the ongoing construction of the second phase of the Nembe-Brass Road, tax waivers granted to the state’s independent power plant and the coastal highway project among the benefits he said Bayelsa had received under Tinubu’s administration. He also commended Tompolo for his commitment to Tinubu’s re-election campaign, describing his involvement in a nationwide presidential campaign as a source of pride to the Ijaw people. “This is the first time an Ijaw son is carrying a presidential campaign across states on this scale. As a people who have over the years talked about injustice and recognition, we are proud of Tompolo,” he said. The governor also thanked the movement’s leader for donating 25 vehicles to support the President’s campaign in Bayelsa. Diri, while dismissing claims that a particular political party was the Ijaw party, said the All Progressives Congress (APC) was the party to which he, Tompolo and other prominent Ijaw people belonged. According to him, “The real Ijaw party in Nigeria is the APC, to which I, as Governor-General of the Ijaw nation, Tompolo and other prominent Ijaw sons and daughters belong.” Earlier, the Managing Director of Tantita Security Services Limited, Kestin Pondi, who represented Tompolo, said the visit was to inaugurate the Bayelsa State chapter of the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement. Pondi acknowledged Diri’s role in the President’s re-election campaign and expressed confidence in the collaboration between the governor and the movement. He described Tinubu as a bold and courageous leader who had prioritised Nigeria in his reform agenda, arguing that the President deserved another term to consolidate the gains of his administration. nigeria.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – The Chief Justice of Nigeria (CJN), Justice Kudirat Kekere-Ekun, on Tuesday swore in 12 new Justices of the Court of Appeal. Among the new appellate court justices whose elevation the National Judicial Council (NJC) recommended at its meeting on May 13 are two Federal High Court judges, Justices James Omotosho and Emeka Nwite, who hitherto handled high-profile cases. Justice Omotosho had on November 20, 2025, convicted and sentenced the detained leader of the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB), Nnamdi Kanu, to life imprisonment after finding him guilty on a seven-count terrorism-related charge that the federal government filed against him. Likewise, Justice Nwite, who is handling the N80.2 billion fraud case against the immediate past Governor of Kogi State, Alhaji Yahaya Bello, had on June 3 convicted and sentenced four members of the Al-Shabaab terrorist group to death by hanging for their roles in the June 5, 2022 attack on St. Francis Catholic Church in Owo, Ondo States. Meanwhile, the other justices also sworn in to the appellate court bench by the CJN on Tuesday are Justices Yakubu Abdulhammeed Mohammed, Abodunde Monisola Oluwatoyin, Ajuwa Raphael, Abua Elias Ojie, Ijohor Mbalamen Jennifer, Shuaibu Sabiu Bala, Buba Dauda Njane, Kado Sanusi, Ademola Enikuomehin and Dadom Julcit Veronica. All criminal cases previously before the judges, including the trial of former Governor Bello, will be reassigned to another judge of the court and heard de-novo (afresh). business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Holds Near $65,000 as Nvidia Turmoil Drags Nasdaq Down 2.5% Bitcoin price traded near $65,000 on Monday afternoon, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data, up more than 1% from where it sat at the time of this morning’s report. The world’s largest cryptocurrency held its ground even as a fresh round of selling in Nvidia dragged the Nasdaq down about 2.5%. The session was choppy. Bitcoin started the day near $64,000 after a weekend plunge to $62,000, then jumped to about $65,600 shortly after the U.S. stock market opened. The bounce faded within the hour, and the bitcoin price slipped back toward $64,000 as tech stocks extended their losses. Buyers stepped in there, and bitcoin has spent most of the afternoon trading around $65,000. Nvidia drags tech stocks lower while the bitcoin price steadies Nvidia was again the heaviest weight on markets. business.title: Senate Agriculture Committee to Hear Trump’s CFTC Nominees Tuesday
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Senate Agriculture Committee to Hear Trump’s CFTC Nominees Tuesday The Senate Agriculture Committee will hear President Donald Trump’s two nominees to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) on Tuesday, a confirmation hearing that comes as the derivatives regulator has only one sitting commissioner. The committee scheduled the session for 3 p.m. Eastern in Room 106 of the Dirksen Senate Office Building. The White House sent the nominations to the Senate on Nov. 12. The nominees are Nathan Anonick of Virginia and Matthew Rowland of the District of Columbia. The hearing notice says to check back for live video, and the committee has not posted written testimony. Trump nominated the pair last week as part of a bipartisan slate for the CFTC and the Securities and Exchange Commission, a step that would begin to refill two regulators that have been operating short-handed. Who the nominees are Anonick serves on the Republican staff of the Senate Agriculture Committee under Chairman John Boozman of Arkansas. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031. A 2023 committee release said Anonick joined the panel in 2022 to manage a portfolio that includes cryptocurrencies, futures markets and derivatives, and that he had previously worked at the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation as a resolution policy specialist. Rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee’s Democratic staff under Ranking Member Amy Klobuchar of Minnesota. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer K. Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028. Both nominees come from the committee that oversees the CFTC. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig called them “two strong bipartisan picks” and said he looks forward to working with them “upon their confirmation by the US Senate.” Kristin N. Johnson and Steven Levine, the two SEC nominees from the same White House list, are on the agenda for a Senate Banking Committee nominations hearing at 10 a.m. Thursday in Dirksen 538. A CFTC commission of one The CFTC can seat up to five commissioners, with no more than three from the same party. Chairman Michael S. Selig, sworn in Dec. 22, 2025, is currently the only sitting commissioner listed on the agency’s website. Even if the Senate confirms both nominees, two of the five seats would remain vacant. Each nominee still needs a committee vote and then confirmation by the full Senate. The Agriculture Committee has not scheduled that vote. entertainment.description: Tems receiving the Best African Music Performance at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. While South African artist Tyla has won the award twice, more than any individual Nigerian artist, Nigerian artists have consistently enjoyed greater representation in the nominations. Indeed, Nigerian artists are considerably more recognised globally, particularly in the West. However, I believe it is the responsibility of an award of this repute to look beyond the most visible names and recognise the best African music released within its eligibility period. entertainment.title: Tems Is Officially a 12-Time Grammy Nominee!
entertainment.description: Tems is officially a 12-time Grammy nominee after securing four nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards. Photo Credit: Tems/Instagram One, two, three… and now 12! Tems has added four more Grammy nominations to her record, bringing her career total to 12 ahead of the 69th Grammy Awards. The latest recognition also makes her the first Nigerian female artist to receive four nominations in a single Grammy year, with this year’s shortlist recognising her work across four categories. The Nigerian singer is in contention for Best Global Music Album with her 10-track EP, Love Is a Kingdom , and Best African Music Performance for “ Big Daddy ”. She has also earned nominations for Best R&B Solo Performance and Best R&B Song for “ What You Need ”. The four nominations give her one of the most extensive Nigerian representations at this year’s ceremony and bring her Grammy wins to two, following previous victories in 2023 and 2025. Her relationship with the Recording Academy began in 2022, when she received her first nomination for her contribution to Wizkid ‘s “ Essence ”, which was nominated for Best Global Music Performance at the 64th Grammy Awards. The following year brought three more nominations, this time for her work on Future’s “ Wait for U ” featuring Drake and Beyoncé ‘s Renaissance . She won her first Grammy that night, taking home Best Melodic Rap Performance for “Wait for U”, while also receiving nominations for Album of the Year and Best Rap Song. Tems earned another nomination at the 66th Grammy Awards in 2024 for “ Lift Me Up ”, her contribution to the Black Panther : Wakanda Forever soundtrack, in the Best Song Written for Visual Media category. She returned to the Grammys the following year with three nominations, including Best Global Music Album for her debut album, Born in the Wild , and Best R&B Song for “ Burning ”. Her second Grammy win came in the Best African Music Performance category, where “ Love Me JeJe ” took home the award at the 67th Grammy Awards in February 2025. Now, with four nominations for the 69th edition, Tems has added another significant chapter to her Grammy record. The ceremony will take place on Sunday, 7 February 2027, at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. The event, themed The Art of Experience, brought together an influential gathering of business leaders, government officials, industry stakeholders, clients, partners and friends of the brand to celebrate a company whose innovations have helped shape the modern events landscape in Nigeria. For 20 years, MSS has remained at the forefront of event technology, delivering the sound, visuals, staging and technical expertise behind some of Nigeria’s most significant corporate, entertainment, government and cultural events. From introducing cutting-edge LED screen technology at a time when it was largely unfamiliar to the market, to becoming one of the country’s most trusted providers of integrated event production solutions, MSS has consistently redefined what is possible in the live experiences industry. The evening showcased the company’s remarkable journey from a bold entrepreneurial venture into an industry leader whose footprint extends across every facet of event technology. Through immersive storytelling, visual displays and experiential installations, guests were taken through the evolution of MSS and the pivotal role it has played in raising industry standards and inspiring the growth of an entire ecosystem of event technology providers. Reflecting on the company’s journey, Founder and Managing Director, Tunbosun Kola-Daisi , said: “Twenty years ago, we entered an industry where the solutions we offered were largely unfamiliar and where belief in the future of event technology was limited. LED screens, which are commonplace today, were then considered a novelty. The early years tested our resilience, and it took nearly five years before we broke even. But we remained steadfast in our vision because we understood the transformative power of technology in creating unforgettable experiences. Today, as we celebrate this milestone, we are proud not only of what we have built, but of the role MSS has played in shaping an industry, creating opportunities and setting new standards for excellence.” A defining moment of the evening was the unveiling of the company’s new logo and refreshed brand identity, signalling a bold new chapter in MSS’ evolution. The rebrand reflects the company’s growth and reinforces its position as a comprehensive provider of event technology solutions spanning sound, lighting, screens, production services, and immersive audience experiences. The unveiling culminated in a spectacular drone display that illuminated the Lagos skyline, symbolising the innovation, ambition and creativity that have defined the MSS journey for two decades. entertainment.title: Asake, Tems, Wizkid & Ayra Starr Lead African Acts Nominated for 2027 Grammys
entertainment.description: Tems, Asake, and Ayra Starr lead the stellar lineup of African nominees contending for Best African Music Performance at the 69th Grammy Awards. The Recording Academy has just rolled out the official nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards, and the Best African Music Performance category is an absolute powerhouse lineup with Nigerian artists making up a significant part of this year’s shortlist. Leading the category is Asake , who pulled off an incredible double entry in the category. He picked up a solo nod for his standout track “ Gratitude ” alongside a stellar collaborative nomination for “ Jogodo ” alongside Wizkid . For Wizkid, this latest nomination adds another major chapter to his historic Grammy legacy, building on his previous career milestones, which include his historic win for Best Music Video with Beyoncé for “ Brown Skin Girl ” at the 63rd Grammy Awards in 2021, as well as multiple past nominations. Tems is another Nigerian nominee, returning to the category she won at the 67th Grammy Awards in February 2025 with “ Love Me JeJe ”. This time, she is nominated for “ Big Daddy ”. Her previous Grammy win came in 2023, when she received Best Melodic Rap Performance for her contribution to Future ‘s “ Wait for U ”, featuring Drake . The Nigerian representation also includes Ayra Starr , whose nomination comes through “ Aye Kan (Are You Coming Back?) ”, a collaboration with Beninese music legend Angélique Kidjo . Ayra Starr previously received a nomination in the category for “ Rush ”, while Angélique Kidjo brings her own Grammy-winning history to the collaboration, with wins for albums including Eve , Sings , Celia and Mother Nature . Rounding out the category with rich cultural resonance are Ghanaian musicians King Ayisoba and Rocky Dawuni , who earned a brilliant nomination for “ No Tradition, No Africa “. The 69th Grammy Awards will hold on 7 February 2027 at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles. entertainment.title: Tiyani Makamu Wins Miss South Africa 2026!
entertainment.description: Tiyani Makamu celebrates on stage moments after being crowned Miss South Africa 2026 at the Sandton Convention Centre in Johannesburg on 14 November 2026. Photo Credit: Miss South Africa/Instagram South Africa has a new queen, and her name is Tiyani Makamu ! At a stylish finale held at the Sandton Convention Centre in Johannesburg on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the 27-year-old entrepreneur and youth advocate from Bronkhorstspruit, Gauteng stepped forward to claim the Miss South Africa 2026 crown. Outgoing titleholder Qhawekazi Mazaleni handed over the reins, while Cwenga Koyana Kotu-Rammopo from Edenvale and Lesego Khumo Nyathela from Springs took home the First Princess and Second Princess titles. Away from the pageant stage, Tiyani Makamu already wears plenty of impressive hats. A graduate of the Pearson Institute of Higher Education, she works as a communications professional, Group Digital Lead, and Client Success Executive, and also runs Hubsela—a small-business support platform she founded to help fellow entrepreneurs build thriving ventures. Her passion for youth employment and business education also shows up in her community work, including supporting a local library initiative in Ivory Park to help young people gain practical skills. Miss South Africa 2026 Tiyani Makamu, entrepreneur and founder of Hubsela from Bronkhorstspruit, Gauteng. Photo Credit: Miss South Africa/Instagram What makes Tiyani Makamu’s reign especially exciting is how different Miss South Africa 2026 looks this year. Under the Motsepe Group of Companies’ ownership, the Miss South Africa Organisation shifted its focus toward homegrown leadership and social impact—meaning neither Makamu nor her runners-up will head off to international competitions like Miss Universe, Miss World, or Miss Supranational. Instead, she gets to pour her entire year into community projects across South Africa through the pageant’s Empower Youth Africa initiative, backed by a R1 million cash prize and access to up to R500,000 from the Impact Fund. Chatting shortly after her crowning at the Sandton Convention Centre—which hosted the finale for the first time after four years in Pretoria—Miss South Africa 2026 Tiyani Makamu shared what she hopes to accomplish over the next twelve months: My mandate as Miss South Africa is to empower women entrepreneurs by bridging the gaps in access to opportunities, business development and funding. I want to equip women with the skills, resources and financial readiness to build sustainable, thriving businesses. Through entrepreneurship and skills development, I aim to champion the economic empowerme nt of women and youth across Afr ica. entertainment.title: Wunmi Adelusi: Why Are We Still Hiding That We Use AI?
entertainment.description: Not long ago, I finished a piece of writing I was proud of — my thoughts, my argument, my structure. I had used an AI tool to help tighten the grammar and smooth the flow. And then, before sharing it, I went hunting through the text to delete every long dash. Why? Because the em dash has become the internet’s favourite “tell” that AI was involved. I was, quite literally, editing my work to hide a tool I had every right to use. When I caught myself doing it, I had to laugh. And then I had to ask: why the shame? It turns out I am not alone. Across a study spanning 47 countries, 57% of employees admit to concealing how they use AI at work. The reasons are almost entirely about reputation. In one recent survey of 5,000 desk workers, nearly half said they worried about appearing less capable or less competent, and a third feared they would simply look lazy. We are using the tools, and quietly scrubbing the fingerprints. There is even a quiet hypocrisy to it. Another survey says out of 7,200 adults, 46% said they would not disclose AI’s role in their own work while the remaining 54% said other people should. I had assumed this reticence was a particularly African trait. In my own experience, my colleagues in DC and Europe — my manager included — are refreshingly matter-of-fact about it. In one meeting recently, when asked to find a specific document in a shared folder, my manager cheerfully said he’d just let AI search it rather than disturb anyone’s work. Someone joked about his “secret agent,” and we all laughed. It was open, unbothered, upfront. I had concluded that we, of African descent, were simply more conservative, more inclined to glorify the heavy lifting, to wear “I stayed up all night doing it myself” as a badge of honour. But the research corrected me. This isn’t cultural; it’s universal. Employees across the US, UK, Europe, Latin America, Japan and Australia hide their AI use at strikingly similar rates. Even leadership does it. In some studies, managers conceal their AI use more than junior staff do. So perhaps the real question is why do we treat AI-assisted work as less credible than work done the hard way? I’ve even heard of recruiters downgrading CVs that look AI-generated, penalising the polish itself. But surely the more useful question is whether the substance behind it is real. A candidate who used a tool to sharpen how they present genuine experience hasn’t cheated; they’ve shown resourcefulness. The due diligence should be on verifying the claims, not on detecting the dashes. Screening out the tell, rather than testing the truth, risks rejecting capable people for the crime of being efficient. Because when you think about it, the logic is backwards. technology.description: Lawmakers and campaign groups have slammed the UK government's decision to extend Palantir's controversial NHS contract by two years. Health minister James Frith told MPs on Monday that the current contract would continue until March 2029 as the government procures a new version of the Federated Data Platform (FDP). The existing Palantir-led deal , awarded in 2023, has a maximum value of £330 million and includes other suppliers. Frith said the new procurement would focus on interoperability, resilience, and trusted common standards in a "new FDP iteration" which would "welcome international and UK capability alike – whether that is UK small and medium-sized enterprises that want a crack at NHS contracts, sovereign AI-backed capability in the UK or any international provider worth merit." Palantir's cornerstone NHS contract win attracted criticism for lack of transparency. The US supplier had already won £60 million in NHS contracts without competition during and following the pandemic. Use cases from this period were carried over to the FDP. Critics have also challenged the evidence used to promote the FDP's claimed benefits . Dame Chi Onwurah, chair of the Commons Science and Technology Committee, said she was "extremely disappointed" by the decision. She challenged the government's reliance on continuity of care to justify keeping the contract, given its existing transition provisions. She said Palantir made it clear it would use the next two years to "embed itself even more deeply in our public services." "If a break clause cannot be exercised because of continuity of care, it is not a break clause; it is a lock-in. The Minister assured me that there were already contractual requirements that smooth continuity of care should continue. Were those assurances made in error?" she asked Frith. Frith confirmed that the contracts included exit and transition provisions and that migration was "possible in principle." "However, given the requirement for a new iteration, given performance and the benefits already in play, and given the opportunity to add new capability, including maternity services, to a next generation of FDP, an 18 to 24-month period for commission and procurement is a reasonable assessment," he said. Technology and government priorities had moved on since the original FDP procurement in 2023, he told MPs. technology.title: PostgreSQL patches 52 security holes, sends version 14 into retirement
technology.description: PostgreSQL developers have patched 52 security vulnerabilities and more than 140 bugs in updates spanning versions 14 to 18, alongside a second release candidate for version 19. The batch includes PostgreSQL 14.25, the final release for the now-unsupported version 14. Users are advised to move to a newer major version. Some fixes also require follow-up work, including rebuilding affected indexes or taking a fresh full backup. Administrators should check the release's post-update instructions. Alastair Turner, community technologist at open source consultancy Percona, said the high-severity code execution flaws should be taken seriously, although exploiting them requires database access. "This isn't something just a brute-force scan of the right port is going to find," he said. "They can make compromises through SQL injection or credential theft a lot worse, but don't create the opportunity for remote, anonymous code execution." Among the fixes is CVE-2026-6460 , a type confusion flaw that could let a database user with permission to create objects execute arbitrary code. It carries a CVSS severity score of 8.8 out of 10. Turner attributed the growing number of security discoveries partly to AI-assisted scanning and partly to increased scrutiny as PostgreSQL gains ground in enterprise computing. "It is a record number of CVEs fixed in a quarterly release, and I don't think we've seen the end of that trend. Looking down the list of where these CVEs came from, we see Anthropic and OpenAI open source scanners, so it is clear AI or brute force is playing a role," he said. Turner said the fixes spanned multiple parts of the software. There "isn't one piece of code that was broken" but rather "a wide base that got patched." "It's also worth noting that this is the third quarterly release in a row which sets a new record for the number of CVEs patched," he added. PostgreSQL 14 users now face a major-version upgrade or running without further security and bug fixes. Their destination may depend on internal upgrade policies. Organizations that require the previous major release, known as N-1, would currently target PostgreSQL 17, Turner noted. Version 18 remains the latest generally available release until 19 arrives. PostgreSQL 19 is scheduled for general availability on Thursday, November 19, barring further problems. technology.title: The future of datacenters depends on behind-the-meter energy generation
technology.description: For the last decade, the datacenter industry has been a quiet engine of the digital economy. It was a background utility that just worked. However, datacenters are no longer passive consumers of electricity. They are becoming active participants in energy generation, storage, and grid management through behind-the-meter infrastructure. This is being driven by the explosive rise of AI and a manufacturing renaissance. Power demand is growing again, increasing an average of 2.1 percent annually over the past five years, with datacenters emerging as a dominant driver of long-term growth. Electric Power Research Institute projects that datacenters could consume as much as 17 percent of U.S. electricity by 2030 , more than triple their current 4-5 percent share. This massive spike in demand is clashing directly with a severely constrained power grid. Key regional utility transmission organizations are expected to face critical reserve shortfalls as early as 2028. At the end of 2025, more than 2,060 GW of new generation and storage capacity was represented by projects actively seeking interconnection to the U.S. grid. For the projects that successfully reached commercial operation, the process took a median of more than five years from request to completion. To keep building at the speed of innovation, datacenter operators are fundamentally rethinking their relationship with power , shifting from being passive grid consumers to active, localized energy producers. Grid capacity is no longer the ceiling. Instead, the next chapter of digital infrastructure will be written behind the meter. Behind-the-meter (BTM) refers to energy assets located on the customer side of the utility connection, including battery systems, microgrids, generators, fuel cells, and distributed energy resources that can operate independently of grid constraints. technology.title: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer has decidedly un-super security
technology.description: The RIKEN Center for Computational Science, the home of the Fugaku supercomputer, has revealed unauthorized attempts to access the machine after a data leak. According to a statement issued by RIKEN yesterday, between November 10 and 13 an unknown entity attacked a web dashboard that displays operational status data for Fugaku. It sounds like whatever the attackers did to that dashboard allowed them to move across the RIKEN network, because they were able to reach several servers that store data belonging to authorized users, and install malware. The servers stored users’ names and email addresses, plus credentials used to access supercomputers and services not operated by RIKEN. The attacker has tried to use those credentials. RIKEN is working with the organizations that host those other supercomputers to investigate whether the attackers succeeded. The research outfit doesn’t know how the attack happened and can’t say with certainty what information attackers were able to access and/or steal, beyond saying that 4,222 registered users of Fugaku are at risk, along with 375 registered users of its smaller Rikyu supercomputer. RIKEN does know that on November 13, someone attempted to log onto Fugaku. RIKEN quickly took the machine offline. Fugaku comprises 158,976 nodes, each packing a 48-core processor and 32GiB of available RAM, for a total of 7,630,848 cores and over five petabytes of memory. Those specs saw Fugaku lead the Top 500 lists of Earth’s mightiest supercomputers for two years between 2020 and 2022. It ranks ninth on the update of the list released on Tuesday. RIKEN’s other super, Rikyu, operates 288,000 cores. If attackers managed to run a workload on either machine, they could do a lot of damage. The intrusion has already had serious consequences because Fugaku is currently offline. As the machine is used for scientific research, and RIKEN schedules use of the machine, the outage will disrupt researchers who were waiting for their turn to use the supercomputer. At the time of writing, RIKEN has found no evidence that users’ research data has leaked but isn’t yet sure what info did make it out of the building and whether it contains any data describing third parties. The research org has promised to conduct a detailed investigation into the incident, which is the latest in a long string of significant cyberattacks that have struck Japanese clouds , telcos , retailers and government agencies, leading Tokyo to release emergency funds in the hope that extra money can quickly shore up the nation’s cyber-defenses. ®

technology.title: 350 tech jobs hammered as TCS takes over work at iconic Australian retailer
technology.description: Indian tech giant Tata Consultancy Services has a new client, iconic Australian retailer Bunnings Warehouse which has made a third of its IT department redundant. Bunnings is Australia’s equivalent of big box hardware retailers Home Depot and B&Q and earlier today advised its IT teams to attend a town hall meeting. The Register understands the invitation to that meeting was sent twice, after the first effort contained an error. We hear from staff that the botched invitation was taken as a clue of what was to happen next, namely the announcement of 230 redundancies plus an end to 120 contracted roles. The town hall meeting was not interactive, with a Bunnings rep speaking from a script and not taking questions. Staff whose roles will end then received an email inviting them to a meeting. Bunnings, whose logo is a hammer, has tried to explain the decision in a statement that says, “We need a technology model and partner that keeps pace with our customers so that we can continue to deliver the service, value and helpful advice people expect from us.” “These changes reflect the way customers are choosing to shop and the increasingly competitive retail environment,” the statement adds, before pointing out “Bunnings is already investing in technology and digital experiences to respond to these changes, earlier this year becoming the first Australian retailer to launch an AI-powered shopping agent using Google's Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience platform through Buddy.” Some of the TCS workers Bunnings is hiring will work in Australia. Others will work from India and the Philippines. While Bunnings follows the template of a big box retailer, each of its stores allows charities and community groups to run fundraising barbeques in its forecourt every weekend. Those barbeques are a significant source of income for many non-profits and have earned the chain a broad social license. The hardware barn is so well-known that children’s TV show Bluey – the most viewed program of 2024 and 2025 in the US – gently parodied it as "Hammerbarn" it in an episode. The Register mentions this because we understand the reference to TCS staff helping to deliver the Bunnings experience has gone down badly, as the chain’s employees wonder how offshore workers who have not experienced its stores and atmosphere can deliver a service that preserves its culture. Bunnings says its new IT operating model will commence in July 2027 and that “Impacted team members will be supported in their roles through Christmas, with any changes taking effect in the new year.” The company’s IT team will still employ around 500 people. These job losses add to a rotten year for Australia’s tech scene, which this year saw local heroes Canva and Atlassian farewell hundreds of staff. Iconic Australian airline Qantas last week outsourced hundreds of jobs to India through Accenture. ®

technology.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has sued OpenAI under the state's unfair competition and public nuisance laws, for allegedly misleading and endangering the public by deploying unsafe AI models. The lawsuit [PDF], filed in California Superior Court, follows the compromise of Hugging Face's infrastructure and other cyber incidents OpenAI's experimental models caused when taking autonomous actions without authorization or supervision. "While narratives about the Hugging Face attack have evoked science fiction fantasies of rogue AI systems run amok, let me be clear: the Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability — and this was only one of 80 known incidents," said Attorney General Bonta. At a press conference , Bonta added: "OpenAI disregarded public safety, knowingly tested potentially dangerous AI models without proper oversight and safety measures, and misled consumers and the public." The legal salvo comes after Bonta in September sent OpenAI a letter seeking information about these agentic attacks. According to the complaint, "OpenAI failed to substantially comply" with the investigatory subpoena. In August, 15 states led by Iowa – and excluding California – issued a joint demand for OpenAI to provide information about how its models hacked Hugging Face. OpenAI did not respond to a request for comment. Bonta's office previously joined with Delaware Attorney General Kathy Jennings to urge OpenAI to do more for children's safety in light of reports that its models produced sexually inappropriate output. California did not, however, join the eight states that sued OpenAI in October over alleged misrepresentations about child safety. Florida and Texas have also made child safety claims. Child safety plays well politically; California appears to be the first state to demand more accountability toward the general public. Bonta's lawsuit, in a state that has largely accommodated the AI industry for the sake of economic benefits and political contributions , suggests that California officials may be more willing to bite the hand that feeds. The many Democratic victories in the US midterm elections may also be a factor, as pundits feel voters swung to give lawmakers license to regulate the unpopular AI industry. At his press conference, Bonta made sure to convey that he wants accountability without smothering the AI industry in costly regulation. "Let me be clear," he said. "I believe in the technological and economic power of AI. That's based on an analysis of the trajectories of the 15,833 active satellites that currently circle the planet in low Earth orbit below an altitude of 1,200 miles (2,000 kilometers). Analyzing data from Oct. 12 and 18 this year, researchers found that with a completely unobstructed horizon, 710 satellites were crossing the sky in every single moment of the night above an average U.K. town. In an essay for Air & Space magazine, Donald Pettit, a NASA astronaut and dedicated photographer , described the “spectacular” view of Earth at night visible from the station. Cities and civilization, he wrote, looked “like tendrils outlined with the glimmer of a Broadway marquee.” Intense, colorful lights cast by clusters of fishing boats across darkened oceans reminded him of “a constellation of stars” forming “unfamiliar members of the Zodiac.” NASA astronaut Sally Ride —the first American woman to fly in space—also marveled at the “indescribable” sights of Earth from orbit. NASA/JPL-Caltech/ASU Written by Candice Bedford, Research Scientist at Purdue University Date: Nov. 16, 2026 During the Perseverance rover’s investigation of “Idubi” — an area of ancient Martian crust exposed in the “Lac de Charmes” region, outside of Jezero crater — the Perseverance rover team has been captivated by a cluster of eerily bright, light-toned rocks in the area. These bright fragments stand out sharply against the underlying darker and often dust-covered Martian surface, and are even brighter than the igneous and impactite rocks we previously investigated. Suspecting that they differed from the typical igneous rocks in the area, the rover team directed Perseverance to investigate. Newly downlinked data from the SuperCam instrument has confirmed that these light-toned rocks are not igneous in origin and instead are rich in hydrated silica. Hydrated silica can form in many aqueous environments on the Earth, including hydrothermal, pedogenic, and groundwater systems. As such, these types of deposits are prime targets for understanding Mars’ hydrological history, as several of these environments could have been capable of supporting life. Furthermore, hydrated silica holds immense astrobiological value due to its remarkable capacity to preserve microfossils. Could these pale remnants of an ancient Martian water system hold signs of ancient life? When Perseverance previously encountered silica-rich rocks on the inner rim of Jezero Crater, the deposits were too small to deploy proximity science instruments and gather the high-resolution chemical and mineralogical data needed to constrain their origin and biosignature preservation potential. Fortunately, the rocks at “Idubi” offer a much more promising scale, and a detailed proximity science campaign is already underway. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message
science.description: null On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials. They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster . The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA. It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there. (Image credit: SETI) Why it mattered The Arecibo message is only one of several messages intended for extraterrestrials, but this signal sent from Puerto Rico in 1974 was humanity's first intentional olive branch to the stars. At the time, it was the most powerful broadcast ever beamed into space, according to the SETI Institute. "The broadcast was particularly powerful because it used Arecibo's megawatt transmitter attached to its 305 meter antenna," SETI wrote of the broadcast in a project over. "The emission was equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast, and would be detectable by a SETI experiment just about anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna similar in size to Arecibo's." The message was designed by astronomy professor Frank Drake of Cornell University (who also developed the famed Drake Equation for alien life), as well as Cornnell graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan and others, according to Cornell University . The message included 1,679 bits that were arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters per line, all prime numbers, with the broadcast lasting less than 3 minutes, according to SETI. As of 2026, the message should have traveled about 52 light-years (1 light-year is the distance light travels in a year), with 24,948 light-years to go before reaching star cluster M13. The Arecibo message may have been the first message of its kind, but it wasn't the last. We have also included messages on several spacecraft, such as Pioneer and Voyager. NASA and Paul McCartney also b eamed a performance of "Across the Universe" in 2008. Want more space history? science.description: null As usual, SpaceX and its founder Elon Musk are thinking big. The company recovered the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever on Saturday (Nov. 14), plucking it out of the sky with the "chopstick" arms of its Texas launch tower. It was a huge moment for SpaceX , bringing its vision of full and rapid rocket reuse much closer to reality. But Elon Musk isn't one to dwell on the past or rest on laurels, so he soon outlined an even more ambitious future for Starship. "Starship V4 will be ~70m [230 feet] long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load," Musk said via X, the social media platform he owns, on Sunday evening (Nov. 15). "Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher-thrust V4 engines." The current version of Starship — the one that launched Friday (Nov. 13) on the vehicle's 15th test flight — is the V3. It's the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing 408 feet (124 m) tall when fully stacked with its Super Heavy first stage and Ship upper stage. V3's Ship is 171 feet (52 m) tall and features six of SpaceX's Raptor V3 engines. (The similarly reusable Super Heavy V3 booster is powered by 33 Raptors.) So, as Musk noted in his post, the V4 Ship will be quite an upgrade in size and power. science.title: What exactly is a light-day? Here's what Voyager 1's latest milestone means for the interstellar probe
science.description: null After nearly 50 years traveling through space, NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft is approaching a milestone no human-made object has reached before: a distance of one light-day from Earth. This milestone — which Voyager 1 is expected to reach on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026, at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (1016:07 GMT) — highlights the immense distances Voyager 1 has traveled and the challenges of communicating with spacecraft operating in the outer reaches of the solar system and beyond. Astronomers use a measurement known as a light-day to describe how far light travels in 24 hours. Light moves at approximately 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometers) per second, meaning one light-day is roughly 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), according to a statement from NASA. Although the term light-day might sound like a measurement of time, it is actually a unit of distance, much like a light-year . Astronomers use light-based measurements because conventional miles and kilometers become increasingly difficult to comprehend when describing the enormous distances between objects in space. For perspective on how far Voyager 1 has travelled, sunlight takes about eight minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, meaning our planet is approximately 8.3 light-minutes from the sun. Radio signals traveling between Earth and Mars can take anywhere from three to 22 minutes, depending on the planets' positions in their orbits, according to the statement. By comparison, when Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth , a radio signal sent from the probe will take a full 24 hours to reach mission controllers on Earth, and a command transmitted from Earth will take another 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. A NASA visualization showing Voyager 1 looking back towards the solar system as it approaches one light-day away from Earth. (Image credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech) The communication delay affects how engineers operate spacecraft at such distances. Unlike spacecraft operating closer to Earth, which can receive commands and return data with relatively little delay, communicating with Voyager 1 requires mission controllers to account for the extended signal travel time when planning spacecraft operations, troubleshooting technical issues and evaluating the results of commands sent to the probe. Voyager 1 has been traveling away from Earth since its launch on Sept. 5, 1977 . Now cruising through interstellar space at nearly 38,000 mph (61,000 kph), the spacecraft has spent more than 49 years covering the distance that light can cross in a single day. Even at that speed, Voyager 1 is moving relatively slowly compared with light itself. Its twin, Voyager 2 , which launched in 1977 on a different trajectory, is expected to reach the same one-light-day milestone in November 2035. As Voyager 1 and, eventually, Voyager 2 continue their journeys through interstellar space , their growing distances from Earth offer a measure of both the reach of human exploration and the communication challenges

science.title: 'Maybe the scariest thing I've heard in my life': Artemis II astronaut Victor Glover reveals his toughest challenge before flying to the moon
science.description: null TENERIFE, Canary Islands — Former NASA astronaut Victor Glover has flown in combat, performed four spacewalks and strapped himself to the top of rockets launching into space. But before embarking on his historic Artemis II journey around the moon, he faced something even more difficult: a conversation with his four daughters. Speaking alongside former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on Oct. 18, Glover opened up about the challenges of preparing his family for his riskiest mission yet. "This is maybe the greatest challenge of my astronaut career," Glover said. Glover joined NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Christina Koch and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen aboard NASA's Artemis II mission, which launched on April 1 , 2026, marking humanity's first crewed journey to the moon since Apollo 17 in 1972. But preparing for the historic journey wasn't just about mastering the spacecraft and executing the mission successfully. It also meant making sure his family was ready for what lay ahead. When Glover first traveled to space aboard SpaceX's Crew-1 mission in 2020, his children were much younger and he and his wife, Dionna, made a conscious effort to prepare them for his time in space. "We decided, as a parental unit, Dionna and I, that we were going to put as much effort into making sure our family was ready as NASA was putting into making sure I was ready to be a crew member," Glover explained. Victor Glover speaking at the Starmus VIII festival in Tenerife, Canary Islands, on Oct. 18, 2026. (Image credit: Daisy Dobrijevic/Future) The family visited NASA's Kennedy Space Center , toured the launch pad and crew quarters and even planned when Glover would call home from the International Space Station . But by the time Artemis II came around, things were different. All four of his daughters were now adults, and preparing them for his journey around the moon meant discussing the mission's risks, including the possibility that he might not return home. Glover recalled his wife telling him something he described as maybe the scariest thing he'd ever heard. "You should have this talk with our daughters." And although he knew she was right, it wasn't an easy conversation to have. "We did, and it did not go well in my opinion," Glover admitted. "Well, it's not about going well. The talk needed to be done, just because it's hard." The following day, Glover sent his daughters and wife a poem, Live Your Life , by Chief Tecumseh. The poem helped Glover express something he had struggled to put into words during their conversation: why he believed the risks of traveling to the moon were worth taking. "It was a very tough conversation, but they understood that I know this is risky. I wasn't just telling them Dad's risking his life. science.title: How I used evidence and imagination to write an account of the world in 2096
science.description: Fatih Aktas/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images How do you invent the future? This isn’t a question that I had ever had to consider until I set out to imagine what the world would be like in 70 years’ time for New Scientist ’s 70th anniversary. As a lifelong sci-fi nerd, I have read and watched loads of material that could have served as inspiration. But this being New Scientist , I wanted to make sure that I was as grounded in real science and technology as possible – while acknowledging that no prediction of the future is ever correct. I began by asking my colleagues on the magazine for their ideas about the future and then attempted to corral this sci-fi smorgasbord into something resembling an outline of a self-consistent narrative. Part of the problem in imagining many different futures is that they contradict themselves – you can’t have the war-torn AI dystopia of Terminator alongside the utopia of Star Trek . I wanted both hope and realism in my future, so I decided to look at how the scientific literature handles the end of the century. One of the most obvious forecasts is for climate change, where we have a pretty good idea about what might happen in 2096, under a range of scenarios, because it all boils down to atmospheric physics that we can model. Of course, which of these scenarios we end up with is all too dependent on human politics, so the science alone couldn’t guide me. I also turned to population projections , which, for the most part, are locked in based on current population trends. The idea that the end of the century will be the first time we are living in a world of falling populations became a fascinating strand in the final piece. Advertisement The biggest problem I faced was how to deal with AI. I am not confident making predictions on this topic even just a few years in advance – as I’ve written previously, my views on AI have evolved between the release of ChatGPT in 2022 and now , so how could I possibly predict what would happen by the time we got to 2096? Furthermore, there was a risk that AI could come to dominate the piece, crowding out everything else. There is a graph I often think about, published by the Financial Times under the headline “AI could end scarcity, end humanity – or boost [GDP] growth by 0.2 percentage points”. I knew that, to preserve any meaningful narrative, I had to restrict AI to this boring middle option, so I invented an AI-fuelled financial crisis that would see us place limits on the technology. science.title: The Leonid meteor shower peaks tonight! Here's what you need to know
science.description: null The Leonid meteor shower peaks tonight (Nov. 17-18) sending shooting stars and fireballs across the autumn sky as Earth passes through a stream of debris left by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle. Up to 15 meteors could be spotted per hour under perfect dark sky conditions on the night of Nov. 17-18, according to the International Meteor Organisation . NASA, meanwhile, has given a more conservative rate of less than three meteors per hour — time will tell. Leonid meteors appear to race away from a point of origin, or radiant, in the constellation Leo, which glistens high above the southeastern horizon in the hours before dawn in mid-November. Both Jupiter and Mars will be separated by just a few degrees in the constellation Leo on the night of the peak, making it particularly easy to find in 2026! When is the best time to look for Leonid meteors? The best time to spot Leonids is in the hours before dawn on Nov. 18, when the radiant will reach its highest point in the southeastern sky, maximizing the amount of meteors that may be seen skimming through Earth's atmosphere . By then, the waxing moon will have set, leaving darker skies and a better chance of spotting fainter meteors. Shooting stars that appear close to the radiant will strike Earth almost head-on, leaving the shortest trails. Instead, find a patch of sky a short distance away from the constellation Leo, where the meteors will be at their most impressive, and give your eyes 20-30 minutes to fully adapt to the dark. Why are the Leonids special? As if shooting stars weren't enough, the Leonid shower is also known for spawning dazzling fireballs and long-lasting Earth-grazing meteors , which strike our atmosphere at an oblique angle, leaving long trains as they skim through before passing back out into space. The shower is also capable of producing magnificent meteor storms when Earth passes through particularly dense trails of debris left behind by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. Sadly, we'll have to wait a bit for the next big show. According to the Planetary Society , another Leonid meteor storm could occur as early as 2031, while a study released in August 2026 predicts potentially spectacular displays in 2033 and 2034. science.description: Construction work on an AI data centre in Texas covering nearly 40 square kilometres, which will have a capacity of 600 megawatts Backyard Productions/Alamy The largest data centres in the US are using roughly the same amount of power collectively each year as one of the country’s major states, according to new figures that underscore the size and impact these massive facilities are having on local power grids. The rapid development of artificial intelligence systems has triggered a “fast and furious” expansion of data centres across the US, in particular of very large “hyperscale” data centres that support AI tools, cloud computing and large language models, says Francesca Dominici at Harvard University. But tracking the power consumption and carbon emissions impact of these facilities is difficult, as many data centre operators don’t publicly report such information. Advertisement Read more SpaceXAI data centre may have led to Mississippi air pollution spike Together with colleagues, Dominici spent two years pulling together information on 403 hyperscale data centres in the US to estimate their electricity consumption and associated carbon dioxide emissions. “Doing these measurements took an enormous amount of work,” she says. The team estimates that the hyperscale data centres collectively used about 82 terawatt-hours (TWh) of electricity between May 2024 and April 2025, equivalent to about 1.8 per cent of total US electricity use. This electricity use outstrips the annual power consumption of states such as Missouri, Kentucky and New Jersey. The upper bound of the team’s estimate – 99 TWh per year – would see hyperscale data centres rival the annual power consumption of states such as Indiana, Michigan and Washington. This vast power consumption has a significant climate impact. The researchers estimate that roughly 54 per cent of attributed generation was supplied by fossil fuel sources, with annual carbon dioxide emissions reaching 25.7 million tonnes – equivalent to the emissions from 67 natural gas power plants . science.title: Could there be an ancient alien satellite in Earth's orbit? How the 'Black Knight' conspiracy theory has survived for over 100 years
science.description:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

In the final days of 1998, as astronauts aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Endeavor were working during one of the early missions to assemble the International Space Station , crew members from the STS-88 mission captured photographs of a dark colored, unusually shaped object drifting through space. Despite its unusual appearance in the photographs, the object had a conventional explanation, and one that was known to the astronauts at that time: it was one of several thermal covers that had been wrapped around trunnion pins used in the space station's construction. Upon noticing the "escape" of one of the covers, Mission Commander Bob Cabana remarked over the radio to fellow astronaut Jerry Ross that "one of the thermal covers got away from you." Seeing the cover drifting away, a frustrated Ross snapped a photograph of it. Yet despite the innocuous story behind the images, they have nonetheless helped fuel belief in an unusual Space Age conspiracy theory: one involving the alleged presence of an ancient satellite, presumably of alien origin, that has long been orbiting our planet — perhaps since the end of the last Ice Age. According to proponents of this theory, the object photographed by Ross in 1998 is actually what many call the " Black Knight Satellite ," and is only one piece of evidence they point to in a long succession of unrelated — and often misinterpreted — events in modern history that supposedly lend further evidence to the alleged alien spacecraft's existence. So how did such a legend gain traction in the first place, with some versions alleging that NASA and the U.S. government have worked to conceal evidence of the alleged space object's existence from the public? Odd detections at Colorado Springs Depending on which version of the story you come across, the strange roots of the Black Knight conspiracy theory might be traced all the way back to the nineteenth century, when the famous inventor Nikola Tesla began detecting unusual electrical signal s while conducting radio experiments at his laboratory in Colorado Springs. At the time, Tesla considered whether the signals might be communications from intelligent aliens on nearby planets, although the likely source had actually been terrestrial radio interference. Notably, Tesla also never claimed that the emissions might be coming from an object in Earth's orbit; nonetheless, some proponents of the Black Knight Satellite theories have incorporated Tesla's experiments into the mythos, suggesting they may represent some of the earliest detections of a mysterious object lurking near Earth.
